translation.title: Indometacin Adhesive Patch
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory relief of osteoarthritis (degenerative arthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, epicondylitis of the humerus (such as tennis elbow), muscle pain, and swelling and pain after an injury.
translation.usage: Apply it to the affected area twice a day.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you have experienced asthma, bronchospasm, rhinitis, or angioedema when taking aspirin or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, if the user is a child under 14 years of age, or if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy or breastfeeding. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if you are in the first or second trimester of pregnancy, or if the user is a child. Do not use it on skin with lesions (haemorrhagic skin disease, eczema, infected lesions, burns, wounds), on the eyes, or on mucous membranes. Use it externally only. Do not use an occlusive dressing. Warmth, swelling, flushing, anaphylaxis, photosensitivity, a burning sensation, irritation, dryness, numbness, gastrointestinal discomfort, headache, dizziness, skin reactions, bronchospasm, a drop in blood pressure leading to shock, or aseptic meningitis (headache, nausea, vomiting, fever, a stiff neck, clouded consciousness) may occur. If any of these occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Itching, redness, rash, contact dermatitis, or eczema may occur occasionally. Store at room temperature.
